name: W30 Morning Flow — McGill's Big 3, Straddle and Hip-Flexor Lunge Return
description:
The daily 15-minute opener. **The work block becomes McGill's Big 3 this week** — curl-up, side plank, bird dog — the three that build trunk stiffness without loading the spine, which is exactly what a week of squats, hinges and one-armed baby carrying asks for.

**The stretches rotate back to two that have been away for a month:** the straddle sit for the adductors and the hip-flexor lunge for the front of the hip. Inchworm and world's greatest stretch open instead of the down-dog work.

**Use the readiness screen, not the calendar.** If cossacks and lizard feel open, run the whole thing. If they feel sticky, keep the anchors and drop one work-block move. Five honest minutes still counts.

sets.name: ☀️ Through the Day — Small and Often (Not Now)
sets.notes: Not part of the morning sequence — these are the reminders that get sprinkled through the day.

exercises.notes: Once an hour if you can. Heels down, easy breathing, a little deeper each time.
30s each foot. Let the **ankle** do the correcting, not the hip. Fingertip on a wall is fine on no sleep.
Heel glued down, knee over the toes. **No measurement this week** — the baseline is banked (right 1.5 fists, left 1 fist) and the re-measure is about a month out. Just do the reps.
Sole turns **outward** against the band, shin still. The left one is the point.

sets.name: Primer — Open the Hips and Spine (~3 min)
sets.notes: Keep moving between shapes rather than settling into holds. The long holds come at the end, when you are warm.

exercises.notes: Hands walk out to a plank, then feet walk to the hands. **Legs as straight as the hamstrings allow** — this is the hinge waking up, not a core exercise.
30s each side. Deep lunge, elbow to the instep, then open the chest to the ceiling. **Hips and thoracic spine in one shape** — back after a month away.
Tight fists, thumbs tucked, hinged slightly forward. **This is the brace the squat is asking for** — wake it here so it is available later.

sets.name: Work Block — McGill's Big 3 (~5 min)
sets.notes: Activate, do not fatigue. **These three are the classic trunk-stiffness set** — one resists flexion, one resists side-bending, one resists rotation. Together they cover every direction the spine needs to refuse, and none of them load it.

exercises.notes: **The greasing set — one quick set, never to failure.** Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up.** A daily habit, not a training stimulus.

**Big 3, part one.** One knee bent, hands under the low back, lift only the head and shoulders a couple of inches. **The low back never flattens into the floor** — that is the whole difference from a sit-up. Slow, and breathe.

**Big 3, part two — anti-lateral-flexion, the direct counter to carrying a baby on one hip.** 30s each side. Stack shoulders and hips, drive the bottom hip up, neck long. Drop to the knee if the shape breaks.
**Big 3, part three — anti-rotation.** Opposite arm and leg reach long, hips stay level. **Imagine a glass of water on your low back.** Slow; a rushed bird dog is just arm waving.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Hip + Adductor Arc (~7 min)
sets.notes: Goes last because warm muscle stretches deeper. One continuous arc, not a list of holds.

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Thoracic rotation and hip flexor in one shape.
45s each side. Deep lunge, both hands inside the front foot. Forearms if the hip allows.
**Your readiness screen.** Slow, deep, heel down. Read it as a delta against your own normal — the old ankle sprain means a stiff day here is not a bad-session forecast.

**Back after a month.** Sit tall, legs wide, walk the hands forward from the hips rather than rounding the back. **The adductors are the tissue that capped the wide-stance squat test** — this is their slot.

45s each side. Half-kneeling, back knee down, **tuck the tailbone under and squeeze the back glute** before leaning in — without the tuck you are stretching the low back instead. The undo for hours of sitting and holding.
45s each side. Finish here. Let the hips settle before the day starts.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)
sets.notes: Pick only the block that matches today. Two or three moves, not the whole list.

exercises.notes: **Push day.** 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
**Push day. Rehab anchor.** Thumbs up, lift from the mid-back — the neck stays out of it.
**Push day. Rehab anchor.** Arms stay straight; only the blades move.
**Pull day. Rehab anchor.** Easy decompression before loaded pulling.
**Pull day. Rehab anchor.** Pack down first — the elbows do not bend.

**Pull day — it worked, so it stays.** One light set before the pull-up bar, then **hold a light DB still at about 90° for 30 seconds.** The hold is the new part: a still, moderate load is the calmest thing you can give an irritable tendon, and it goes in before anything hangs off the elbow.
**Pull or KB day. Rehab anchor.** Elbow pinned to the ribs, light or no weight.
**KB day. Rehab anchor.** Ribs down; only the range that stays smooth.
**Legs day.** Toe to wall, heel glued down. No measurement this week — just the reps, before the heels go up on the plates.
**Legs day.** 30s each side for the lateral chain.

tips: Five honest minutes beats a skipped fifteen. Anchors first: cossack, lizard, the push-up set.
The Big 3 are slow on purpose — a rushed bird dog is just arm waving.
No knee-to-wall measurement this week; the baseline is banked until roughly mid-October.
If the cossacks read sticky, keep the flow and drop a work-block move rather than rushing the stretches.
